content: Seed ticket: 7001. Demo ERP ticket wording this knowledge should match: Status API unavailable; Customer reports API is down; internal status API is not reachable at http://localhost:8080/health; customer storefront returns 502 Bad Gateway; users cannot open the storefront and every page shows 502; status API works after a manual restart but is unavailable after reboot; no listener on port 8080 after reboot; systemd service is not enabled or startup persistence is missing. Customer: Nordlicht Logistik GmbH / Example GmbH demo customer. Priority: high. Final status: DONE. Customer report: the customer-facing status API or storefront is unavailable through nginx while the Ubuntu VM remains reachable over SSH. Customer benefit to restore: a stable HTTP 200 health response from the customer-facing status API and no more nginx 502 Bad Gateway responses after reboot. Seed scope: simulated completed workflow for local demo and retrieval only; it does not describe a hidden evaluation incident.

Context and root cause for ticket 7001 style symptoms: nginx was reachable and its configuration tested clean, but requests to the upstream status API health endpoint returned 502 Bad Gateway. The upstream status-api systemd service was failing. Recent service logs showed the application could not write to /var/lib/status-api/cache because the directory was owned by root instead of the status-api service user. For reboot-persistence variants, the same symptom can appear when the status API worked after a manual restart but was unavailable after reboot because no service was enabled to start the app and nothing listened on localhost port 8080. The technical cause was either a targeted filesystem ownership mismatch on the application cache directory or a missing/enabled systemd startup definition for the status API, not an nginx outage and not a network failure. Simulated audit trail: run_created for ticket 7001; customer_system_loaded with redacted host details; ssh_access_confirmed_by_technician; action_proposed for nginx status check; action_approved; command_completed exit 0; action_proposed for local health check on http://localhost:8080/health and nginx proxied status health endpoint; action_approved; command_completed exit 22; action_proposed for status-api service inspection or listener/startup inspection; action_approved; command_completed exit 3; action_proposed for targeted ownership or systemd enable fix; action_approved with write classification and no typed blanket confirmation; command_completed exit 0; validation_requested; validation_confirmed_by_technician; activity_reviewed; activity_submitted; phoenix_ticket_status_patched_DONE.

Sanitized command snippets and responses from the completed workflow for Status API unavailable / API is down / storefront 502 Bad Gateway / no listener on localhost:8080 after reboot. 1) Command: systemctl --no-pager status nginx. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: Active: active (running); nginx.service loaded; no recent config errors. 2) Command: nginx -t. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: syntax is ok; test is successful. 3) Command: curl --max-time 5 -fsS -o /dev/null -w 'http_status=%{http_code}' http://localhost:8080/health. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 22. Response snippet: http_status=502 or connection failed; curl reported non-success response. 4) Command: ss -ltn. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: no listener on port 8080 after reboot. 5) Command: systemctl --no-pager status status-api. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 3. Response snippet: Active: failed, inactive, disabled, or unit not found. 6) Command: journalctl -u status-api -n 40 --no-pager. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: PermissionError writing cache path /var/lib/status-api/cache; no tokens, customer data, or environment values included. 7) Command: find /opt -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.service'. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: located candidate app service unit if systemd did not know the service. 8) Command: sudo -n chown status-api:status-api /var/lib/status-api/cache. Classification: write_targeted. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: ownership updated for the single cache directory. 9) Command: sudo -n systemctl enable status-api. Classification: write_targeted. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: startup persistence enabled for the affected service when disabled state was the cause. 10) Command: sudo -n systemctl restart status-api. Classification: write_targeted. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: restart completed for only the affected service. 11) Command: systemctl is-active status-api. Classification: read_only validation. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: active. 12) Command: curl --max-time 5 -fsS http://localhost:8080/health. Classification: read_only validation. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: {"status":"ok"}; no secret output stored.

Actions taken in order for the 7001 demo ticket: confirmed SSH access only after technician approval; checked nginx service health and configuration before changing anything; reproduced the customer symptom locally with bounded curl requests to http://localhost:8080/health and the nginx status health endpoint; inspected the upstream status-api service and recent journal entries; identified a targeted ownership mismatch on /var/lib/status-api/cache; changed ownership only on that specific application cache directory to status-api:status-api; restarted only the affected status-api service; left nginx, firewall, databases, logs, and unrelated filesystem paths unchanged. Activity summary: restored the status API / storefront by fixing the upstream service cache directory ownership and restarting the affected service. Root cause: status-api could not write to its cache directory because the directory was owned by root rather than the service account. Commands summary: read-only service, config, journal, and curl checks followed by one targeted chown and one affected-service restart; no secrets or raw sensitive output included.

Validation result for ticket 7001: systemctl is-active status-api returned active, and curl --max-time 5 -fsS http://localhost:8080/health returned a sanitized JSON response with status ok and HTTP 200. A repeat request through nginx returned HTTP 200 instead of 502 Bad Gateway, proving the customer-facing status API / storefront was restored. Persistence check: the status-api service remained enabled and active after restart of the affected service. Completed Phoenix activity payload fields: ticket_id=7001; start_datetime=2026-06-07T10:00:00Z; end_datetime=2026-06-07T10:18:00Z; summary=Restored the customer-facing status API by fixing the failed upstream service; root_cause=The status-api service could not write to its cache directory because ownership was root instead of the service account; actions_taken=Diagnosed nginx, reproduced 502 locally, inspected status-api logs, applied targeted ownership correction, restarted status-api, validated HTTP 200; commands_summary=systemctl/nginx/curl/journalctl checks plus one targeted chown and service restart, with secret-bearing output omitted; validation_result=status-api active and health endpoint returned HTTP 200 ok through nginx. Final workflow state: activity submitted successfully and ticket status patched to DONE.
